text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak: Moslems today are at a crucial crossroads and the only choice available to them is development and renewal. The president speaks at the festival marking the Night of Quranic Revelation, says those who diverged to extremism tried to impose an intellectual terrorism on the whole society that has no relation whatsoever to religion.
- Mubarak and French President Chirac hold telephone discussion on international and regional issues as well as the Middle East peace process.
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat lauds Mubarak's peace efforts.
- Mubarak returns safely to the homeland after an effective Egyptian performance at the Davos forum.
- General Authority for Investment approves 280 million pound project to reclaim 30,000 acres (12,000 hectares).
- Mubarak says that the modern call for Islam begins with reclaiming the soul and society and reviving morals.
- Thousands of Kuwaitis are arriving in Egypt to spend the Eid al-Fitr holidays.
- Seventy-three Israeli soldiers killed in a helicopter collision.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says Egypt is against the partition of Sudan and will not give military aid to Zaire.
- Government to give 3,000 pounds ($882) to the families of each victim of the Edfu train crash.
- Seventy-three Israeli commandos killed in helicopter collision. The planes were on their way to bombing Lebanon.
- Speaker of parliament says there were no political motivations behind lifting the immunity of the Labour MP.
- Prosecutor releases five Satanists, still detaining 25.
